description: GroundwaterDupuitPercolator is a Python groundwater-flow component distributed with Landlab. It solves a Boussinesq approximation for a shallow unconfined aquifer and calculates groundwater return flow to the land surface. Users supply a grid, aquifer-base and ground elevations, recharge, hydraulic conductivity and porosity. Outputs include water-table elevation, aquifer thickness and discharge fields. It can support simplified groundwater availability and runoff calculations around drinking-water or irrigation systems, with the application geography and resolution determined by the user. The component documentation and the parent GitHub repository are public; the Landlab code is MIT licensed. Its main limitation is the Dupuit-Forcheimer approximation, which assumes a laterally extensive, relatively thin aquifer and a small capillary fringe. Surface-water routing requires another component. No directly related catalogue record was established; the earlier CSDMS Workbench draft only names the broader Landlab package. This metadata review did not run the component or assess a real aquifer. The code is available free of charge under its stated licence.
